summary.tagline: Rago National Park (Norwegian: Rago nasjonalpark) is a national park in Sørfold Municipality in Nordland count

travel.headline: Check visitor access before departure

days.title: Storskog Valley and Central Waterways
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Storskogvatnet
stops.detail: North of Storskogvatnet there are also some willows, rowan shrubs, alpine blue-sow-thistles and globeflowers.

stops.name: Storskogdalen
stops.detail: The Storskogdalen runs from Lakshol in the west to Storskogvatnet in the northeast.

stops.name: Storskogelva
stops.detail: The Storskogelva (also called Nordfjordelva) flows through pine forests and through the Storskogdalen through the park.

stops.name: Trollfossen
stops.detail: Also well-known is the Trollfossen below the Storskogvatnet with a drop of over 100 meters (despite its name, it is not located in the Trolldalen).

days.driving: Allow time between these sights; local travel times are not verified and conditions vary.

days.title: High Plateaus and Waterfalls
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Litlverivatnet
stops.detail: The largest lakes are Litlverivatnet and Storskogvatnet.

stops.name: Værivassfossen
stops.detail: The largest waterfall is the Værivassfossen (also called Litlverivassfossen), which falls 223 meters deep from Litlverivatnet into the Storskogdalen.

stops.name: Ragotjahkka
stops.detail: The Ragotjahkka is at 1,312 meters above sea level the highest mountain in the national park.

days.title: Northern Valleys and Southern Ridges
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Trolldalen
stops.detail: The Trolldalen lies somewhat isolated in the north of the Rago.

stops.name: Lappfjellet
stops.detail: In the south, a long mountain ridge dominates, featuring the Lappfjellet and the Flatkjølen, which extends to Sweden.
